Bill.BriefDescription: Prohibiting the administration of credit card applications on campuses of institutions of higher education.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to prohibiting the administration of credit cardapplications on campuses of institutions of higher education; adding anew section to chapter 28B.10 RCW; creating a new section; andproviding an effective date.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: The legislature finds that eightyonepercent of students have received a credit card by the end of the firstyear of college, and that the high interest rates on student creditcards, coupled with their ease of use and a poor understanding of howcredit works, often leads to runaway and unmanageable debt. Thelegislature also finds that students routinely apply for credit cardssimply to get free merchandise, but two or three years later, studentsmay begin to receive collection notices for credit cards they requestedbut never received or used. Students in North Carolina who seekassistance from student legal services about debt problems own anaverage of four and seventyseven onehundredths credit cards with anaverage balance of seven thousand dollars each. This amount of creditcard debt is in addition to any loans the student is obligated to payback after graduation. The legislature further finds that many states p. 1 HB 1934have found success in regulating credit card companies' ability tosolicit business from college students by controlling the conditions ofsoliciting and mandating certain behavior from the institutions ofhigher education. Lawmakers in ten states have introduced legislationto try and rein in credit card companies' solicitation of collegestudents and to increase students' access to educational programs aboutcredit and financial management. The purposes of this act are toencourage young adults to obtain credit cards in a more responsiblemanner and to keep young adults out of credit card debt. Thelegislature finds that due to the first amendment rights in the UnitedStates Constitution, this act cannot prohibit the soliciting of thecredit card companies, but will ban the administering of credit cardapplications on college campuses.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 28B.10 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) Institutions of higher education shall ban the administrationof credit card applications on site of a college campus and shallencourage young adults to establish credit in a more responsiblemanner. (2) The definitions in this section apply throughout this sectionunless the context clearly requires otherwise. (a) "Ban" means to prohibit, not allowing without any exception,not having any right to do so, and banishing the right of. (b) "On site of a college campus" means on any and all propertyowned by the institution of higher education itself, within any bordersof the belonging property of the institution. (c) "Administering" means the act of handing out or giving to, orallowing one to get a hold of an application. (d) "Application" means any form or piece of information thatallows one to apply or sign up for a credit card, and any way and/ormeans that commits a student to the credit card requirements or itscommitments.

If any provision of this act or itsapplication to any person or circumstance is held invalid, theremainder of the act or the application of the provision to other HB 1934 p. 2 persons or circumstances is not affected.
